pm_exper_user_586_maasv_v0446_pmv2_r1.all_options:
(a) Since you experience seasonal allergic rhinitis from pollen, you could head to cultural festivals in paved city squares rather than grassy fields, and wear stylish wraparound sunglasses to keep pollen out of your eyes. It’s a way to still enjoy vibrant spring events while managing your symptoms.
(b) Since you get seasonal allergic rhinitis from pollen, you could plan outdoor time right after rainfall when pollen counts drop, and wear wraparound sunglasses while cycling or walking. Choosing paved park paths over grassy fields can also help you enjoy spring without the sneezing.
(c) To enjoy outdoor time in spring without discomfort, you could go for walks after it rains and choose areas with less plant density. Wearing sunglasses and sticking to paved routes can also make the experience more pleasant.
(d) Because you tend to react to pollen in spring, try timing your walks or bike rides for early morning after it rains, when the air is clearer. A light scarf or mask can also keep airborne pollen from making you uncomfortable while you’re out.
